verified_facts_for_writer.clean_core_extensibility_levels: SAP formalized a four-level model (A-D) in Aug 2025, evolving the older 3-tier model. Level A: released APIs only (ABAP Cloud on-stack or side-by-side on BTP), fully upgrade-safe, target for new dev. Level B: classic ABAP using only officially provided APIs/frameworks (legacy APIs, BAdIs, user exits) - allowed when Level A cannot meet the need; needs governance. Level C: uses SAP internal/unclassified objects, not cloud-ready, meaningful upgrade risk, belongs on a remediation roadmap. Level D: explicitly non-recommended (modifications, write access to SAP tables, implicit enhancements) - highest risk, eliminate. Source: SAP Community 'ABAP Extensibility Guide - Clean Core for SAP S/4HANA Cloud - August 2025 Update' + SAP News 2025/08.
verified_facts_for_writer.sap_cloud_alm: SAP Cloud ALM hosts the 'RISE with SAP Methodology Dashboard' which surfaces Clean Core compliance KPIs (custom object count by level, ATC exception log, new exceptions since last review, remediation roadmap for Level C/D). ATC clean-core check results can be uploaded to this dashboard. Source: SAP Community 'Enhance Clean Core Compliance: Activate Your RISE Dashboard in SAP Cloud ALM' + 'New Clean Core Extensibility KPIs arrive on the RISE with SAP Dashboard'.
verified_facts_for_writer.atc: Central ATC (ABAP Test Cockpit) in the SAP BTP ABAP environment is SAP's recommended approach for governing ABAP development for clean core in S/4HANA private cloud / on-prem. New clean-core ATC checks (e.g. ABAP_CLEAN_CORE_DEVELOPMENT variant) published Aug 2025; supports exemptions workflow + baseline. ATC can run in blocking mode for high-priority findings. Source: SAP Community 'ABAP Test Cockpit (ATC) recommendations for governance of clean core ABAP development'.

history_snapshot.why_distinct: All 5 existing articles treat clean core as a MIGRATION-TIME event (define it, clean Z-code once, assess readiness once, place extensions, choose brownfield/greenfield). None covers the ONGOING-DISCIPLINE problem: how the core drifts BACK to dirty after go-live and the governance operating model (board/CoE, ATC blocking + exemption log, SAP Cloud ALM KPI cadence, transport governance, MDG) that prevents it. This is a post-implementation OPERATIONS angle, not a migration angle. The A-D levels appear only as governance INPUTS (what to monitor/approve), not as a maturity score (that is -03's job), keeping subtopic Jaccard < 0.4 against all five.
